site.name: Matchless Mine
site.componentDetail: Historic silver mine complex with No. 6 shaft/headframe, hoist house, powder magazine, and Baby Doe cabin
overview: The Matchless Mine is one of Leadville’s best-known historic silver properties, important both for its role in the mining industry and for its association with Horace Tabor and Elizabeth “Baby Doe” Tabor.
The surviving surface complex preserves recognizable mine infrastructure that helps explain underground extraction, hoisting, ore handling, and daily life at a late-nineteenth-century Leadville mine.

timeline.text: Horace Tabor acquired the Matchless property during Leadville’s rapid silver boom.
The mine operated during Leadville’s major silver-production era and became part of Tabor’s mining fortune.
The national silver crisis damaged Leadville’s silver economy and Tabor’s finances.
Horace Tabor died after the collapse of much of his former fortune.
Baby Doe Tabor remained closely associated with the property and lived at the mine late in life.
The surviving historic site is preserved and interpreted as a surface mine complex.

moreHistory: The property is important both as an industrial mining site and for the Tabor family story.
The surviving complex includes the shaft/headframe area, hoist house, powder magazine, and cabin.
Public interpretation is focused on the surface complex; Remnant does not imply visitor access to underground workings.
